title: One list, three uses
description:
An enum, a function that turns each value into its name, and a count of the values: three things that must always agree. Written by hand, somebody eventually adds a value to one and forgets the others.

The **X-macro** trick keeps one list and generates all three from it. `COLOR_LIST(X)` applies whatever macro `X` you give it to every entry. Define `X` one way to make enumerators, another way to make `case` lines, and `#undef` it after each use.

Inside a macro, `#name` turns the argument into a string: `"red"`.

From `COLOR_LIST`, generate:

- `enum class Color` with one enumerator per entry, in order,
- `constexpr std::string_view toString(Color color)`,
- `inline constexpr int colorCount`.

Do not type any colour name yourself. The tests add nothing to the list, but your code should keep working if someone did.

starter.solution.cpp:
#include <string_view>

#define COLOR_LIST(X) \
    X(red)            \
    X(green)          \
    X(blue)           \
    X(amber)

// enum class Color, toString and colorCount, all generated from COLOR_LIST

hints: For the count, define `X(name)` as `+1`. Then `0 COLOR_LIST(X)` expands to `0 +1 +1 +1 +1`.
rules: Use `COLOR_LIST` three times: for the enum, for `toString` and for the count.
Do not write the colour names by hand; let the list generate them.
